<reason>Side B won by distinguishing scrutiny from liability and showing that knowingly pooling private lease data through a common pricing hub can constitute concerted action. Side A pressed a strong scope objection and defended independent discretion, but never fully answered why regulators should need proof of coordination before scrutinizing the platform where that proof resides, or why a right to deviate defeats scrutiny when cartel members can also cheat.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: joint adoption of the hub can trigger the same inquiry as direct coordination, communication can run through the hub, and holding rents is profitable only if rivals are assured not to undercut.</best_rebuttal>
